kevin: Quick RFC follow-up — we pushed the draft about dynamic headroom for Dedicated GPU pools. Wanted to align on the live behavior we expect when: tenants spike, burst credits are exhausted, and prewarmed nodes are in the middle of draining. TL;DR: propose soft-headroom + prioritized admission + fast-fallback lane.

anya: thanks for the ping. can you recap the soft-headroom idea? i skimmed the rfc but want the concrete runtime actions.

kevin: sure. soft-headroom = keep a small reserve of GPUs that are not committed to steady-state allocation. it's probabilistic: we maintain headroom H per region computed from P95 tail risk and recent spike rate. requests hit admission controller with tenant priority; if total usage > capacity - H, we start admitting into a "burst" class that can use credit. if credits exhausted, lower-priority tenants get 429s or routed to hosted fallback.

saira: how do we compute H? the RFC used a 95th-quantile formula but didn't include decay when traffic calms. we must avoid permanently over-reserving after a one-off blast.

kevin: good point. propose H_t = max(H_min, alpha * P95_window + beta * spike_rate) with exponential decay factor gamma that halves the excess every T minutes. config knobs: H_min, alpha, beta, gamma, T.

tom: can we see pseudocode? easier to reason about.

kevin: ```
# recompute every minute
observed = sample_p95(last_60m)
spike = spikes_per_minute(last_15m)
H_raw = alpha*observed + beta*spike
H_t = max(H_min, H_prev*exp(-gamma*dt) + (1-exp(-gamma*dt)) * H_raw)
```

jonas: admission policy question: when in burst mode, do we still colocate tenants or isolate to burst nodes? isolation reduces noisy neighbor issues but wastes capacity.

anya: I'd prefer dedicated burst nodes per tier if we can afford it. For enterprise tenants we isolate their burst lanes to guarantee no performance regressions for steady tenants. For standard tenants, best-effort colocation is fine.

autoscale-bot: note: dedicated burst nodes will increase 95th percentile cost in our cost model by ~7% for the sample region (simulated). See /sim runs 2026-03-10.

kevin: right — that aligns with cost/perf tradeoff. Two more runtime behaviors to decide: 1) eviction order when prewarming drains and we need to free GPUs for higher-priority requests, 2) how to surface metrics and debug traces for ops.

saira: eviction: prefer evicting from low-priority burst requests first, then from prewarm warmup jobs, then from steady allocations but only if they exceed their burstable window. also prefer evicting shortest remaining time (SRT) to minimize wasted work.

tom: SRT requires we track per-inference estimated remaining time; that's noisy for streaming. maybe track by request class (batch vs streaming) + sample percentiles. Simpler: pick jobs with smallest observed recent throughput or oldest burst session start?

jonas: for stateful cache-warmup workloads, evicting breaks warm caches — we should mark caches as fragile and avoid evicting those unless critical. add "cache_protected" flag to tenant metadata.

kevin: agreed. add tenant metadata: priority_tier, burst_credit_balance, cache_protected boolean, isolation_required boolean.

anya: regarding metrics: need per-tenant admission_decision (admit|burst|reject|fallback), latency impact delta, cost_delta, and a trace id that ties admission -> placement -> GPU node. ops should be able to run a single query to fetch last 1k admission decisions for a tenant.

kevin: we'll add an admission_event log stream tagged with trace_id, tenant, reason, decision, node_id. retention 7 days by default, 30 days for enterprise.

tom: rollout plan? can't flip cluster-wide without canary. propose: implement config flags and simulator, then canary region with 2 tenants at low traffic, then add traffic shaping heatmaps for 48h, then ramp to 20% region traffic, monitor rejection rates and SLA deltas for 7 days.

kevin: yes. also need a safe kill switch: global "admission.mode = off" to revert to current static allocation. and a read-only preview mode that calculates decisions without applying them (dry-run) for 24h.

jonas: how do tenants buy burst credits? in Dedicated product we have pre-purchased monthly credits + overage pool. need to ensure runtime decrements credit on admitted burst usage and replenishes at fixed cadence. Also support manual admin grants.

saira: strong need for consistency when decrementing credits across HA controllers. prefer a single leader per region to mutate credit state, with async replicas. QA case: leader failover must not double-charge. implement idempotency tokens on admission responses.

kevin: +1. we'll add request_id and admission_nonce; leader records nonce for given request_id. if replica handles same request after leader failover, it can consult nonce store.

anya: edge case: long-running streaming requests that hold GPU for > billing window — how count credits? charge by active seconds rounded up to billing granularity and cap per-request max. also support "grace" time for transient network blips (5s).

jonas: we should simulate worst-case: hundreds of concurrent long-running streams on burst lane with exhausted credits — will the admission controller queue or reject? queueing increases latency; rejecting is transparent. I vote for immediate rejection once credits exhausted unless tenant has explicit admin override.

tom: +1. also add a per-tenant queue_limit and queue_ttl to avoid head-of-line blocking.

kevin: next steps I've proposed:
- eng-runtime: implement admission service changes + leader nonce store (2-wk spike)
- eng-sre: run simulator across past 90-day traffic window (1-wk)
- product: define burst credit pricing + enterprise isolation policy (1-wk)
- devex: add trace viewer for admission_event (2-wk)

anya: can someone file an infra task for leader-based credit store? I'll pick up the simulator config.

jonas: I'll file the admission_event schema PR and include trace_id correlation semantics.

kevin: thanks. I'll draft the deploy checklist and the kill-switch config. will post checklist here before Friday.

saira: small nit: include an explicit test for clock skew across controllers in the failure modes doc.

kevin: good call. added.

anya: ack. thanks all, this is a good path forward.

kevin: closing loop — i'll post draft checklist and the alpha config (alpha knobs listed) in #eng-runtime tomorrow. feel free to ping me for quick sync. :thumbsup:
